title: America's AI Action Plan
summary: The AI Action Plan lays out more than 90 federal actions under innovation, infrastructure, and international security pillars. It treats AI leadership as a full-stack problem involving models, scientific data, chips, data centers, power, permitting, workforce, cybersecurity, exports, and secure government compute.
key_findings: AI infrastructure policy includes data centers, semiconductor fabs, reliable power, grid expansion, and skilled trades.
The plan calls for AI-enabled science, high-quality datasets, evaluation, security, and adoption across government.
International policy is framed around exporting complete U.S. AI stacks rather than isolated software.
why_it_matters: It makes the physical and institutional dependencies of AI unusually explicit and provides actions that can be monitored for implementation.
ftfn_relevance: Creates dated follow-up lanes for federal standards, infrastructure, procurement, and export programs.
evidence_limits: The plan contains recommendations and directives at different stages of implementation.
It does not establish that grid capacity, fabs, data centers, workforce, or secure compute have been delivered.
